title: The application exposes a liveness probe endpoint that answers whether the process is stuck
description: The application serves a liveness probe at a stable HTTP path. A 2xx response from the endpoint means the process is running its event loop and is not wedged; a 5xx response means the process is stuck and the orchestrator should restart it. The endpoint's answer never depends on the health of any external dependency: a database outage, a broker outage, or a partner API outage never turns liveness red on its own. The endpoint runs entirely inside the process boundary.
rationale: Liveness is the orchestrator's restart signal. Coupling it to external dependency health causes a database blip to cascade into a full restart storm across every replica, and cascades cause outages that dwarf the original blip. The invariant that liveness answers strictly on in-process state (event loop responsive, main thread not deadlocked) is what makes restart the correct action when the probe fails.
